title: Latency & fallback benchmarks — Weekly check-in (W14 2026)
content:
Summary:

Quick check-in on kernel v2.7.1-rc experiments, KV-cache prefix caching pilot, and dynamic batching changes. This week we focused on understanding a surprising p99 regression after landing the memory-copy micro-optimizations and on validating our new fallback routing behavior under load. We also iterated on observability to make tail latency sources more visible.

Attendees:
- Asha Patel (owner)
- Jonah Kim
- Priya Sharma
- Hector Ruiz
- (logs later include intermittent notes from SRE on-call)

Key metrics (canary cluster, 4xA100, mixed traffic replay of prod trace from 2026-03-30, 90th percentile of traffic):
- Baseline (v2.6.9): p50=28ms, p95=132ms, p99=410–420ms, throughput=115k tokens/s, KV-cache hit ratio=56%
- Kernel v2.7.1-rc (with memcpy micro-opt): p50=22ms, p95=125ms, p99=460–490ms (regression), throughput=122k tokens/s, KV-cache hit ratio=56%
- With prefix-KV enabled (KV pilot): p50=20ms, p95=118ms, p99=440ms, throughput=135k tokens/s, KV-cache hit ratio=64%
- Dynamic batching (auto-batch sizing, memlimit=2.5GB): p50=24ms, p95=130ms, p99=520ms (more tail), throughput=137k tokens/s

Observations:
1) p99 regression after memcpy micro-optimization:
   - Root-cause hypothesis: the memcpy path introduced a scheduling stall for sequences > 2048 tokens in current kernel loop; observed jitter correlated with context length and cache refill paths.
   - Evidence: flamegraphs show CPU wait spikes on worker thread during KV cache refill, and nvprof traces show stalls coincident with memcpy calls on host pinned memory.
   - Related artifact: PR #5678 implements the memcpy change; rolling that patch back on canary reduces p99 back to ~420ms.

2) Prefix KV cache pilot:
   - Enabling prefix caching for the top-50 prompts in replay increased hit ratio to ~64% and reduced request counts toward model by ~12%.
   - Implemented a conservative TTL (30s) and LRU policy; observed a small memory footprint bump (+6%).
   - No correctness regressions observed in our deterministic evals (eval-suite v2).

3) Dynamic batching trade-offs:
   - Auto-batching increases throughput (throughput +18%) but increases tail latency under bursty traffic patterns because of batch wait timers.
   - Tunables that matter most: max_batch_delay, min_batch_size, and memlimit. Current defaults (max_batch_delay=6ms) are too aggressive for low-latency tier.

4) Fallback routing behavior under GPU contention:
   - Canary routing policy tested: primary->fallback model route with capacity-aware fallback. Under simulated GPU preemption, fallback succeeded but introduced additional model-switch latency ~40–60ms due to KV cache warming and model init overhead.
   - Action: try warm standby models with shared KV cache (see action items).

Incidents / anomalies:
- 2026-04-06 @14:12 UTC: observed a 3–4 minute p99 outage on canary when running the memcpy-enabled kernel and KV cache eviction coincided with a traffic spike. SRE paged; mitigation was to roll back the PR. Ticket: JIRA-INF-3421.

Decisions made in meeting:
- Roll back memcpy micro-optimization from v2.7.1-rc on production canary until we have a root-cause fix (Jonah to open rollback PR and coordinate with release engineering).
- Continue prefix-KV pilot in limited clusters and expand coverage to additional high-frequency prompts (Priya to update pilot list).
- Reduce default max_batch_delay for low-latency tier to 3ms and add auto-switching policy when backend p99 > 300ms (Hector to implement).

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Jonah: open rollback PR for memcpy micro-opt and add a postmortem note in JIRA-INF-3421 (ETA: 2026-04-08).
- Priya: expand prefix-KV pilot to 3 more prompt families and generate new hit-rate dashboard (ETA: 2026-04-14).
- Hector: implement dynamic batch tiering (low-latency vs throughput) and default max_batch_delay=3ms for low-latency route (ETA: 2026-04-12).
- Asha: run extended stress tests (24h) with mixed-length traces and capture per-thread blocking metrics, coordinate with SRE for scaling to 8xA100 cluster (ETA: 2026-04-11).
- Jonah + SRE on-call: add host-level memcopy instrumentation and trace correlation to #serving-runtime for faster debugging (ETA: 2026-04-09).

Open research spikes / experiments:
- Prefetching KV pages on request start vs on-demand refill. Prototype shows ~12ms reduction in refill latency for long contexts but increases memory churn; need longer runs.
- Investigate using GPU pinned memory pool to avoid host-device memcpy stalls. Early tests promising but requires cross-team validation with infra.
- Evaluate minibatching heuristics that prioritize oldest requests to reduce head-of-line blocking for latency-sensitive routes (algorithm sketch in confluence).

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider a small guardrail in the kernel: if seq_len > 4096 use an alternate refill path that yields earlier yield points.
- Add a "tail-latency safe" mode for kernels that trades ~5% throughput for stable p99 (useful for enterprise SLAs).
- Add a dashboard card that shows 'delta vs baseline' kernel changes over last 7 days (p50/p95/p99 + KV-hit-rate).
